model.rationale: The district's thirteen-point Democratic lean, Grijalva's roughly ten-to-one cash advantage, and market pricing near 97 percent all point to a safe Democratic hold. With no public polling available, the picture rests on fundamentals, which show little realistic path to an upset.

overview:
Arizona's 7th District is a strongly Democratic seat, and incumbent Adelita Grijalva is running to keep it after securing the nomination. The district's partisan lean of roughly thirteen points Democratic, combined with a favorable environment, gives the incumbent a substantial structural advantage heading into the general election.

Grijalva has raised about $2.5 million and holds roughly $469,000 on hand, while Republican Daniel Butierez has raised about $234,000 with just over $11,000 remaining. Outside spending has been minimal and mostly supportive of the incumbent. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. No public general-election polls are available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
